title: Middle of Linked List
statement: Find the middle node of a linked list.
inputOutputContract: Input n followed by head-to-tail list values, n>=1; if n even, choose the second of the two middle nodes.

mistakes.hint1: Inspect the fast moves only one node behavior in findMiddle; the current algorithm is close, but one operation changes its result.
mistakes.hint2: Start by tracing T1 manually. Watch Node / head / slow / fast at each iteration or recursive return.
mistakes.hint3: Check the invariant of findMiddle: Slow advances one Node and fast advances two; the second middle is required for even length.
mistakes.hint4: Concentrate on the expression or branch that controls this mistake: `fast = fast->next;`. What does it do on the failing input?
mistakes.hint5: Compare the intermediate state with the expected output of T1. The mistake is in fast moves only one node, not merely formatting.
mistakes.hint6: Adjust the faulty operation so that it follows this rule: Slow advances one Node and fast advances two; the second middle is required for even length.
mistakes.hint7: A targeted correction is to replace `fast = fast->next;` with `fast = fast->next->next;` in findMiddle, then retest T1–T6.
